_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the VinceForge capability matrix. Rows are data;
the prose around them lives in docs/capability-matrix.tmpl.md.
converter/selftest_matrix.py  -> asserts every enforced_by symbol still
exists, and that no warning/refusal site
in the code is unclaimed by a row
RULES FOR EDITING (they are the whole point of this file):
* Every row MUST name at least one real code symbol in enforced_by, or
state "none" deliberately. A row with an unsourced verdict is exactly
the inference this project forbids - see CLAUDE.md.
* A verdict changes only when the CODE changes. Never edit a verdict to
match what you believe the tool does; check, then edit both.
* ids are stable and permanent - the Migration Team guide cites them. Renaming

rows.native_note: the fallback: a block that needed the pipeline path but got no --ion-api-base-url (or is an <Export>-only block) is still built here, with the unsupported filter gate left off and a loud warning naming why
rows.pipeline_note: auto-routed per BLOCK, not per-file (a real CustomerA file splits 3 native-safe / 5 needing it across 8 blocks), narrowly: only when a block has a RowFilter native cannot express (build.native_filter_problem - since 2026-09-28 that means a range on a non-numeric value, e.g. CustomerA' '!'; a numeric range stays native). Needs --ion-api-base-url; the other existing native gaps (non-uniform per-transaction filters, an M3-written-column filter, grouping) do NOT trigger it. Predicted at SCAN time too, from a real parse, so the plan and the confirmation box shown before a real (non-dry) import see it - not only a dry run's results. SECOND trigger since 2026-09-29: a native body over app_classic.NATIVE_BODY_SIZE_LIMIT (150 KB) is rebuilt on the pipeline path, because Live refuses oversized workflows ('Item size to update has exceeded the maximum allowed size'); this one is decided at BUILD time only (it needs the built body), so it shows in the results, not the scan
rows.to_change: widen the narrow trigger to the other native gaps, if that turns out to be worth the added Code-step surface - a separate, later decision
